findings.title: Blocked email matching is exact and case-sensitive
findings.body: BlockedEmail.should_block? queries BlockedEmail.where(email: email), and neither the model nor the migration normalizes email case. Discourse treats emails case-insensitively in other places, so a block entry for 'bad@example.com' will not match 'Bad@Example.com'. A blocked user can bypass the block by changing case, and the unique index permits case-variant duplicate block rows.

findings.title: Validation query mutates blocked-email records
findings.body: should_block? increments match_count, sets last_match_at, and saves the record every time it is called. It is invoked from EmailValidator during User validation. UsersController#create calls user.valid? and later user.save, which reruns validations, so one signup attempt can update the blocked-email row multiple times; updates made inside a failing save may also be rolled back while those from a standalone valid? call remain. The counters and timestamps become unreliable, and validation performs database writes. The return value of save is ignored.

findings.title: Non-atomic counter update
findings.body: The match count is updated by loading the row, incrementing it in Ruby, and saving it. Concurrent requests using the same blocked email can lose increments. An atomic increment_counter/update_counters call would preserve the statistic.

findings.title: Domain restriction regex is not anchored
findings.body: email_in_restriction_setting? builds a case-insensitive regular expression from the raw setting after escaping only dots, and it does not anchor the domain's end. With a whitelist of 'example.com', an address like 'user@example.com.attacker.com' can match and be accepted, defeating the whitelist and potentially causing incorrect blacklist behavior.

findings.title: Validator tests stub the blocking logic
findings.body: The EmailValidator spec stubs BlockedEmail.should_block? and only checks whether an error is added. It does not exercise the actual blocked-email lookup, case handling, counter side effects, or the moved whitelist/blacklist domain logic, so regressions in the real validation path are not covered.
